reader.requirement: At --std 85, each symbolic-character-1 without IN is the native character at ordinal integer-1 (ordinal n = code unit n-1 here), and with IN alphabet-name-2 the character at ordinal integer-1 of that alphabet's character code set (NATIVE, STANDARD-1/2, or a literal phrase whose ordinals follow the specification, THRU in either direction, ALSO sharing one ordinal represented by literal-1, unspecified characters implementor-placed after), the IN phrase applying to every name/integer group of its clause; an ordinal absent from the set is refused.

edition-consulted.switches: SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS FOR ALPHANUMERIC/NATIONAL refused at 85 (COBOL0900), admitted at 2023
whether a word in integer-1's place may be a constant-name (2002+); at 85 it is refused as not an integer literal (COBOL1547)
the alphabet an IN phrase names cannot be a 2002 national or LOCALE alphabet at 85

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes, only at the edges: the FOR phrase and constant-name ordinals are refused at 85; the ordinal mapping itself is the same code at every edition.

reader.notes: CodedCharacterSet.CharAt is the one ordinal-to-character map: identity for NATIVE and STANDARD-1/2 (ISO 646 IRV as U+0000-U+007F, documented DOC-A.1-182/187; the 1985 text itself equates the IRV currency sign with $), RepByPos for a literal phrase's specified block and the native-order tail after it. The IN word is read once per clause, so it covers every group.

refuter.evidence: Rendered PDF p.245 plus Errata C124 (outermost braces deleted): [SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS {{symbolic-character-1}... {IS|ARE} {integer-1}...}... [IN alphabet-name-2]]..., so IN closes a clause and each repeated clause has its own IN. r6sym-003: ALPHABET AL IS 90 89 "QRS" 70 ALSO 71; P1 P2 P3 ARE 1 3 5 IN AL = Y Q S; a separate clause P4 IS 66 without IN = native A; P5 IS 6 IN AL = E (only literal-1 of the ALSO pair represents it, GR4d 6); P6 IS 65535 IN AL = U+FFFF (the last ordinal: 7 characters share 6 ordinals, so the set has 65535); P7 IS 128 IN STANDARD-2 = native U+007F. Refusals: r6mid-001 'M1 IS 1 IN AL M2 IS 66' (a group after IN without a new SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS) refused COBOL5506, as the corrected format requires; r6big-001 65537 IN a literal alphabet and 129 IN STANDARD-2 refused COBOL1670 (SR10); r6sym-001 65536 IN AL refused COBOL1670, correct because the ALSO pair leaves 65535 ordinals. The message's '(literal-phrase, 65536 characters)' gives the character count and not the ordinal count, so it hides why 65536 is refused. That is diagnostic text, not this rule. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR8  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR8'; 'OK  §1985:VI.4.5.3 SR10  (4.5.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR10'; 'OK  §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR4d ... the text is in GR4d' (only literal-1 is used); 'OK  §1985:VI.4.5.2  (4.5.2 General Format)  the text is in the clause' (Errata C124).
